x_ranikivav_024: Stepwells gave communities in dry western India year-round access to water, and became places to gather, rest and worship. Rani-ki-Vav, on the banks of the Saraswati river in Patan, is one of the finest.
x_ranikivav_025: It was built in the 11th century during the rule of the Chaulukya (Solanki) dynasty, and is traditionally linked to Queen Udayamati. Its stepped corridors and pavilions carry hundreds of sculptures, many of them of Vishnu and his avatars. Silt from the river buried it for centuries, which helped preserve the carving.
